title: dedicated-gpu-pool-autoscale-warmup-breadcrumbs-11
content:
Quick breadcrumbs/notes from 2026-02-20 -> 2026-02-28 investigating the Dedicated GPU pool capacity thrash during warmup windows. Personal scratchpad; rough commands, outputs, hypotheses, next steps.

Summary of the problem:
- Symptoms: during traffic spikes (model-load events) the dedicated-gpu pool would rapidly scale up nodes but then scale down before pods finished warming (models initializing), causing repeated thrash and request failures. Observed increased p95 latency and 'Insufficient gpu' pod scheduling errors and intermittent 503s.
- Window: incidents spiked around 2026-02-18..2026-02-24 after we shipped the new model-version rollout.

What I ran / raw commands + notes:
1) Check pod events for impacted pods
$ kubectl -n dedicated get pods -l app=redwood-model --sort-by=.metadata.creationTimestamp -o wide
# saw repeated restarts and long initialization times (20-90s) for model containers

$ kubectl -n dedicated describe pod redwood-model-xyz
Events:
  Normal   Scheduled   10s   default-scheduler   Successfully assigned dedicated/redwood-model-xyz to node-gpu-07
  Warning  FailedScheduling  9s  default-scheduler  0/5 nodes are available: 3 Insufficient gpu.com/gpu, 2 node(s) had taints that the pod didn't tolerate.
  Normal   Pulling  7s  kubelet  Pulling image
  Warning  Unhealthy  60s  kubelet  Readiness probe failed: HTTP probe failed with statuscode: 503
Comments: readiness probe failed because model server returns 503 until weights are loaded.

2) Node lifecycle checks (GKE / on-prem logs)
$ gcloud compute instances list --filter="name~'node-gpu-'" --zones=us-west1-b
# Instances spin up in ~60-120s; but kubelet register jitter causes pods to be scheduled only after node Ready + kube-proxy + CRI startup (~30s more)

3) Autoscaler config snapshot
$ kubectl -n kube-system describe hpa dedicated-gpu-autoscaler
# Config shows scaleUpCooldown: 30s, scaleDownCooldown: 60s, minNodes: 0, maxNodes: 20, targetUtilization: 0.7
Observation: cooldowns are short; minNodes=0 allows full drain to 0; combined with long warmup leads to repeated spin-ups.

4) Looked at our warmup hook (init container) behavior
- init-container: pulls weights, untar to /mnt/weights, then exit -> main container starts. Some models download 1.6GB and take ~45-90s on 100MB/s network. No explicit readiness gating until HTTP probe on port 8080 responds OK.

5) Autoscaler logs (excerpt):
[2026-02-22T14:12:09Z] scale-up detected: average-util=0.82 -> adding 3 nodes
[2026-02-22T14:12:11Z] nodes provisioned: node-gpu-11,node-gpu-12,node-gpu-13 (status: provisioning)
[2026-02-22T14:12:45Z] observed pods still Pending due to Insufficient gpu.com/gpu
[2026-02-22T14:13:40Z] scale-down initiated: nodes to remove: node-gpu-11 (idle for 35s)
[2026-02-22T14:13:55Z] node-gpu-11 drained and removed

Result: scale-down triggers before pods finish warmup -> new requests hit no-capacity -> another scale-up -> thrash.

Hypotheses (short list):
- H1: minNodes=0 allows pool to drop to zero causing full cold starts; increase minNodes to maintain a small warm pool.
- H2: cooldowns are too short (scaleDownCooldown 60s) relative to average warmup time (~90s). Autoscaler is too eager to scale down.
- H3: readinessProbe is tied to model being fully warmed; node is considered idle once kube metrics drop even while init/weight load happening because pod isn't counted against utilization until Ready.
- H4: weight download is single-threaded from central object store (S3/GCS) causing slow warmups - we should pre-pull or use local cache layer.
- H5: burst capacity reserved pool not configured (we have a 'burst' flag but it's not wired into policy).

Quick experiments & results:
- Experiment A: bump minNodes=2 in a test pool, keep cooldowns the same. Result: warm pool prevents 503s during a synthetic spike; cost increased ~+8% in test.
- Experiment B: set scaleDownCooldown to 180s (3m) in test; observed fewer thrash cycles; scale-down deferred until nodes fully idle after warmups finish.
- Experiment C: change readinessProbe to delay initial checks (initialDelaySeconds=120) so pod not considered Ready before warm; but that made HPA think pods were not Ready and created more nodes (worse). Conclusion: readiness semantics interact badly with HPA metrics.
- Experiment D: pre-pull weights in a DaemonSet / node-prewarm job on new nodes via startup hook (tested with prewarm script). Prewarm decreased new pod init time from 70s -> 12s but requires bandwidth and disk staging.

Error snippets seen repeatedly:
- "0/5 nodes are available: 3 Insufficient gpu.com/gpu"
- "Readiness probe failed: HTTP probe failed with statuscode: 503"
- "containerd: failed to start containerd-shim: OCI runtime create failed: resource busy" (rare)
- kube-controller-manager log: "evicting pod due to node scale down"

Notes on metrics we monitor (and gaps):
- We were monitoring node CPU/GPU util and pod counts; but HPA is using pod-CPU-based metric on model server which is 0 until ready (so autoscaler undercounts warming pods). Need to use custom metric that counts Pending/Initializing pods or track weight-download-progress metric.
- No metric for "time since node provisioned" vs "time since first pod scheduled" - would help determine warm window.

Immediate mitigations proposed (short-term):
- Increase minNodes=2 for critical dedicated pools (prevents 0->N cold starts).
- Lengthen scaleDownCooldown to 180s (or 1.5x median warmup).
- Add a cheap readiness proxy: an init-step or sidecar that registers the pod as "warming" to autoscaler metric so capacity considers them while warming (or emit custom metric exposed to HPA).
- Enable node prewarm job: on node join, pull top-10 heavy model weights. Tradeoff: disk + egress costs.

Medium-term/engineering fixes:
- Change autoscaler to consider Pending pods with GPU requests as "requested capacity" even if not Ready. (Autoscaler plugin change).
- Add prewarm-tier nodes with ephemeral cached weights and fast-attach storage (local SSD snapshot).
- Improve weight artifact distribution (multi-part parallel download, mirror cache per-region)
- Improve scheduling: prefer pre-warmed nodes for cold start traffic via nodeAffinity / preferredDuringScheduling and podPriority.

Outstanding questions / TODOs:
- Who owns minNodes policy for Dedicated product? Product or infra? (Ticket: JIRA-INC-2026 created)
- Can we add a HPA custom metric that counts pods in Pending state requesting GPUs? Need infra/metrics changes.
- Cost modeling: run cost-benefit for minNodes=2 across all pools (estimate +8% cost vs SLO improvements).
- Run a controlled canary with minNodes=1 and scaleDownCooldown=180s for 24h on us-west pool. (Action: Marco to run canary 2026-02-25)

Quick links & references (for followups):
- Incident JIRA: JIRA-INC-2026
- Infra PR (prewarm script + daemonset): github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/412
- Console dashboard snapshot: console.redwood.ai/dedicated/pool/us-west/warmup-2026-02-22 (internal)

Notes for retrospective:
- We need to codify "warmup time" into autoscaler config as first-class parameter per-pool.
- Warmup should be measured and recorded per model version and exposed to routing/scale policies.

Next steps (short):
- [ ] Merge infra PR for prewarm (small test) -> GH PR 412 (blocked on review)
- [ ] Create canary plan for minNodes=1/2 + cooldown=180s (Marco)
- [ ] Instrument metric: pending-gpu-pods-count (Hannah / infra-metrics)
- [ ] Postmortem draft (skeleton) -> link to Confluence when ready (ENG-4923)

Scratch misc commands to run next time:
$ kubectl -n dedicated get nodes -l pool=dedicated-us-west -o json | jq '.items[] | {name: .metadata.name, age: .metadata.creationTimestamp, conditions: .status.conditions[] | select(.type=="Ready")}'
$ kubectl -n kube-system logs deploy/autoscaler -c autoscaler --since=2h | grep "scale-up" -A3 -B3
$ curl -sS http://model-node:8080/health || echo "health fail"; # verify readiness endpoint behavior

End of breadcrumbs. Will consolidate into a cleaner incident writeup once we validate canary results.

- Hannah
